summary_paragraph: An elderly woman with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, recurrent venous thromboembolism, and long-standing anemia was admitted for fatigue and abdominal pain identical to prior anemic episodes. She presented with a hemoglobin of 5.9 g/dL and was transfused two units of packed red blood cells, after which her symptoms resolved. A CT scan showed no acute abdominal process or bleeding, and her pain was attributed to transient hypoperfusion from anemia. She also received IV furosemide for signs of fluid overload related to heart failure. Her warfarin was continued with a therapeutic INR. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider for CBC monitoring and to continue management of her chronic conditions.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
